//: Copy to config.json and fill in. ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES OVERRIDE EVERY VALUE HERE — the name in each `// <KEY>` note below is the variable that wins over it, from .env or the shell. That is what makes a one-off possible without editing this file: BFMR_MIN_INSURANCE_VALUE=999 python -m sync_tracking. README.md lists all of them in one table. Booleans are true/false in BOTH places; 1/yes/on still parse, but anything unrecognised is false, so a money switch fails closed on a typo.
//2: EVERY setting lives here — nothing is environment-only any more, including the container schedule. .env is purely the OVERRIDE layer, and is where dev/one-off values belong: a temporary LOOKBACK_DAYS, or a host-specific RUN_INTERVAL_HOURS, without touching the config everything else shares.

browser_use.// api_key: BROWSER_USE_API_KEY — required. The cloud browser every scraper runs in (CDP reads, receipt capture, the Costco token grab) — NOT just the agent.

google.// sheet_id: GOOGLE_SHEET_ID — required. The id from the sheet's URL.
google.// worksheet_name: GOOGLE_SHEET_WORKSHEET_NAME — the tab. Created if absent.
google.// service_account: Paste the WHOLE JSON object Google gave you here, then share the sheet with its client_email. GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_FILE still points at a standalone file instead, and wins when set.

alerts.//: Configure at least one channel. With neither, an unattended host reports a logged-out session or a failed run to nobody. Test with `python -m alerts.notifier`.
alerts.// gmail_app_password: GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD — a Google APP PASSWORD, not your account password.

scraping.// lookback_days: LOOKBACK_DAYS — CALENDAR days back, counting today as 0. 1 = today and yesterday.
scraping.// default_cashback_rate: DEFAULT_CASHBACK_RATE — for a card not listed in `cards`. Write 2% as 0.02 or "2%", never 2.
scraping.// amazon_promo_cashback_enabled: AMAZON_PROMO_CASHBACK_ENABLED — add Amazon's per-order 'Earn N% back' promo on top of the card's rate.
scraping.// amazon_gift_card_netting_enabled: AMAZON_GIFT_CARD_NETTING_ENABLED — record every non-card tender an order was part-paid with — gift card, a spent Prime cash-back balance, Amazon points — in the Gift Card column (the COGS formula subtracts it), so no cost or cashback is booked on money the card never spent. false leaves the cell blank and COGS uses the full sticker cost.

buying_groups.// sync_enabled: BUYING_GROUP_SYNC_ENABLED — SPENDS REAL MONEY. On, every scheduled run submits tracking numbers and files BFMR insurance unattended. Leave off until a dry run and a one-package live test have both been done. `python -m sync_tracking` ignores this.

bfmr.//: BFMR authenticates with TWO HEADERS (API-KEY / API-SECRET), not a bearer token. Both from Developer Tools in your BFMR account settings.
bfmr.// min_insurance_value: BFMR_MIN_INSURANCE_VALUE — only insure shipments worth at least this. BFMR charges ~0.45% with a $2.00 MINIMUM, so below roughly $450 the floor dominates and the effective rate passes 1%. 0 insures everything.

mod.//: MaxOutDeals needs a bearer token AND an IP allowlist — add this machine under the firewall tab in your MOD profile, or every call is rejected however valid the token. user_id and email are required in the BODY of every request.

receipts.// capture_enabled: RECEIPT_CAPTURE_ENABLED — the off switch that keeps working credentials in place. `oci.bucket` is the real master switch: blank means capture is completely inert.
receipts.// dossier_upload_enabled: DOSSIER_UPLOAD_ENABLED — also upload each failure dossier (report + page HTML/PNG) under failures/ in the same bucket, so the alert carries a link instead of a path on the host. Same PII class as receipts. Set a 30-day lifecycle rule on the failures/ prefix.

oci.//: Uploads go through OCI's S3 COMPATIBILITY API, so these are an OCI 'customer secret key' (access-key/secret pair), NOT the API signing key.
oci.// par_url_prefix: A Pre-Authenticated Request URL made ONCE by hand in the OCI console (Target: Bucket, Permit object reads, listing OFF). TREAT AS A SECRET — anyone holding it can read every receipt, and a receipt carries your name, address, card last 4 and totals.
oci.// failures_par_url_prefix: A SECOND PAR, for failure dossiers: Target 'Objects with prefix' failures/, Permit object reads, listing OFF. Paste the URL as given (ending /o/failures/). Blank = dossiers are not uploaded. Treat as a secret.

// container: Read by docker/entrypoint.sh on start. These used to be docker-compose-only, because compose interpolates its own file before Python runs — the entrypoint now resolves them from here instead. Irrelevant outside Docker.

container.// run_interval_hours: RUN_INTERVAL_HOURS — hours between scheduled runs. Each run spends one of MaxOutDeals' 10 daily received-items calls, so preflight warns when the interval implies more than that.
container.// run_on_start: RUN_ON_START — also run once the moment the container starts. Handy on first boot.
container.// preflight_strict: PREFLIGHT_STRICT — refuse to start when preflight fails, instead of alerting and running degraded. Off by default: a container that won't start also stops scraping, and a missed order costs more than a degraded run.
container.// timezone: TZ — the cron schedule follows this.

// profiles: One Browser-Use browser identity per entry, each behind its own proxy. `amazon` and `amazon-business` are separate accounts and MUST NOT share a profile — one identity for both is exactly the linking risk the separate profile exists to avoid. `profile_id` is filled in for you by `python -m scripts.create_profile`.

profiles.label: profile-1
profiles.// auth: Username + password, plus a TOTP seed, keyed by retailer. TURN 2-STEP VERIFICATION ON for the account and paste its authenticator secret into `totp_secret` — the deterministic path generates the 6-digit code itself and ticks the 'don't ask on this device' box. Leave `totp_secret` blank only if the account has 2-Step off; a challenge with no seed fails the login rather than falling back to the paid agent, which is never given the seed (a seed is a permanent key, not one 30-second code). Supported for `bestbuy` and `amazon-business`.

profiles.label: profile-2
profiles.// auth costco: Costco sign-in. Its GraphQL data path is browserless and does NOT use this — the browser session is only for minting a refresh token and capturing receipts, and without this block a lapsed browser session needs a human. NO `totp_secret`: Costco has no US 2-step verification, so leave it out entirely (preflight reports OK rather than warning). If Costco ever adds 2FA the sign-in says so by name — see the design notes.
profiles.// auth amazon-business: Amazon Business self-login. Without this block a lapsed session records NOTHING until you re-run scripts/create_profile by hand. `totp_secret` is the base32 key from Login & Security -> 2-step verification -> Authenticator App -> "Can't scan the barcode?" — enrol an AUTHENTICATOR APP rather than SMS/email, because a texted code is one nothing here can receive. Costco needs no auth block: its data path runs on a stored refresh token and opens no browser.

// warehouses: Which buying group an order belongs to, matched on its DELIVERY ADDRESS. A jig is a deliberately misspelled variant the group hands out ('THIRTEEN SAMMPLE DR1VE') so each order routes distinctly — it is a routing token, never a postal address, and nothing ever files it as one. Name a group literally `Personal` to have those rows dropped before the sheet is written.
// cards: Cashback per card, matched on the last 4 digits the scraper reads. `retailer_rates` overrides the card's overall rate at one retailer. Rates accept 0.02 or "2%" — never a bare 2.

cards.// profile: Scopes a card to one profile, when two accounts each have a card ending in the same 4 digits.
cards.name: Personal Amex Gold
